newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-LAST OVER SIX GIVES WARWICKSHIRE DRAMATIC WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LAST OVER SIX GIVES WARWICKSHIRE DRAMATIC WIN.

text.p: A straight driven six by Gladstone Small off ex-England fast bowler Devon Malcolm from the penultimate ball of the match earned Warwickshire a Benson and Hedges Cup Final place in dramatic fashion on Tuesday.
Last wicket pair Small and Allan Donald had needed 12 runs from the last over after Derbyshire had scored 216 for eight in their 50 overs.
Derby looked set to end second in their group, already won by Yorkshire, when they reduced Warwickshire to 193 for nine.
But Small and Donald, who between them had accounted for five of Derby's wickets, then used the bat to good effect, with Small's final blow clinching a one-wicket victory.
Middlesex, who in their opening Cup match were beaten by Ireland, continued their woeful form when they lost by 27 runs to Somerset at Lord's.
Somerset, who were already assured of a semifinal place, made 287 for six, principally due to a 101-run fifth wicket partnership between Peter Bowler (79) and Richard Harden (66).
Middlesex were then bowled out for 260 despuite a fine 77 from Paul Weekes and 60 from Scott Moffat.
